storyboard.ears: Earth never actually stops erupting. It just moves around.
Earth has about 1,400 active volcanoes, but only a tiny slice are erupting at any moment. So the planet always has a few going.
storyboard.evidence: Smithsonian Institution | How many of Earth's volcanoes are active, by definition | https://volcano.si.edu | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Three in four sit along one line, the Pacific Ring of Fire. So the danger is packed around one ocean's edge.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) | Share of Earth's active volcanoes on the Pacific Ring of Fire | https://www.usgs.gov | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Just 16 are labeled 'Decade Volcanoes', the most dangerous to nearby people. Out of over a thousand, that's a short watch list.
storyboard.evidence: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) | All active volcanoes vs officially designated 'Decade Volcanoes' | https://www.usgs.gov | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Something, somewhere, is always on fire under your feet.
